cards.heading: Five circles of closeness to Christ

blocks.text: Jesus Christ chose seventy disciples from among five hundred brethren, twelve apostles from the seventy, three disciples - Peter, James, and John - from the twelve, and one, John, from the three. Each narrowing circle marks a deepening relationship with Christ - {{1co 15:6|1 Corinthians 15:6}}.
Picture it as five concentric circles: the outermost and largest holds the five hundred; inside that, the seventy; inside that, the twelve; then the three; and at the centre, the one.

This outermost circle represents ordinary church members - born again, but following Christ from a distance. They attend church when it's convenient, remain close enough to the world's pull that backsliding comes easily, and in an unfavourable moment, could deny Christ altogether - {{jo 18:18,jo 18:25,jo 18:26,jo 18:27|John 18:18, 25-27}}.

Peter himself followed Jesus from afar off and denied Him when sudden danger came - that's the spiritual standard of this group. Staying here offers no guarantee of endurance to the end - {{prv 9:16,prv 9:17,prv 9:18|Proverbs 9:16-18}}. Sin can look appealing, but its end is death. Many in this group drift, tasting the world, returning, drifting again - up one day and down the next; more often than not, once they fall, they don't return. It's always easier to fall than to stand.
To have tasted the goodness of God and then fallen away is a painful loss, because the joy once known disappears - {{2pe 2:20,2pe 2:21,2pe 2:22|2 Peter 2:20-22}}.
